chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Lionel Hampton's band visits; Prez played chords by ear
summary: Hampton's first band came to hear them rehearse, and Collins learned that Prez knew no chord names yet ran intricate patterns by ear.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: But any way they would all come down to hear us

rehearse, down to Woodside. And they stayed around for awhile, but it was quite an experience playing -- I learned a lot playing with Prez. Well, I mean I -- well, one thing, Prez didn't know chords, but he had an innate sense. He had an ear that was just terrific, you know. He would make an intro by himself, and he would run some of the most intricate patterns you would think that he knew chords. And I would ask him, "now do you know what chords you're playing?" He said, "no." He would just hear them, and it was just intricate patterns. And I could hit a chord, I could make any -- play any progressions and he could play it right away. But he didn't know any chord.

Yeah, he read. Enough to -- not to hurt his playing. You know. But you just have to learn when you play with this calibre of musician, you know, a lot of it rubs off. Then this is why you have to stay in a certain element, a certain level of music to progress, you know. So any way, by working with Prez I came in contact with so many guys that I had heard of, that I hadn't met at this time, because they all -- everybody loved the president, you know.
